steps.text: Preheat the oven to 300 degrees F (150 degrees C).
Mix sugar and flour together in a large bowl. Beat in eggs and butter until well combined. Stir in milk and vanilla until incorporated. Fold in coconut. Pour into prepared pie crust.
Bake in the preheated oven for 1 hour. Cool completely before slicing.

raw_recipe.headline: Coconut Pie
raw_recipe.description: This coconut pie recipe has an easy filling made with flaked coconut and simple pantry ingredients for a sweet and delicious old-fashioned dessert.

video.description: In this video, learn how to make a creamy and sweet coconut pie. This refreshing summer dessert starts by beating sugar, flour, butter, and eggs until well combined. Add in milk, as well as vanilla extract and the flaked coconut to finish the pie filling. After pouring it into the pie crust, bake it for an hour. The pie filling is easy to make and with a store-bought pie crust, this delicious tart is easy for anyone to make!
video.name: How to Make Coconut Pie

review.reviewBody: Yummy pie! I made it for my family and they loved it. I would use maybe 1/4 a cup more shredded coconut, but then again i love coconut a little too much! Very eggy, and very good! I recommend this!

My husband and I did not enjoy this pie very much when we first tried it. The filling was too eggy. I added about 1/2 cup of mini chocolate chips to the filling to make it even more like a Mounds bar and I think it was a good addition. The very edge of the pie, where the filling touched the crust and got the most cooked, was chewy and macaroon-like, and I liked that part. I'm not sure how to get the rest of the pie to be the same, maybe 1 less egg, more coconut and a higher cooking temperature. After refirgeration for 24 hours, I took the remaining pie to the office and everyone was raving about it, so I tried another piece and it was better then it had been the day before.

I made it and it is great, but I did make some changes. I would recommend using a deep-dish pie crust because I had almost a cup of filling leftover from using the regular crust. Second, I used 1/3 cup of butter and 3 tablespoons of whipping cream (unwhipped). I also toasted sweetened coconut

I have made this more than once and I'm getting better at perfecting it. I make dough from scratch and start out at 400 degrees for the first 15 min. Then down to 350 for 30 min. Double coconut and use a cup of buttermilk for milk. I broil meringue and coconut on top for 5 min. It's a family favorite

Pie is awesome! Made a few changes based on reviews from others. Lessened the sugar to 3/4 cup, used 2 eggs instead of 3, and used two cups of sweetened coconut. Mixed the ingredients as directed but split between two pie crusts. Put chocolate chips on bottom of one crust to make a Mounds-like pie. Sprinkled rest of coconut on top of pies.
Cooked for 55 minutes at 325 degrees and checked, then cooked 15 minutes more.
Pies are delicious...not eggy at all. Pie is browned amd pretty. Mounds pie has creamy layer of chocolate at bottom.
Will probably use full cup of sugar next time to see how much sweeter it is. Love this recipe.

I made the pie today for our Christmas dessert. It was tasty and very easy to put together but when I fix it again, I will use half regular milk and half evaporated milk to make it more creamy. Plus, I would prebake the pie crust a little.. It was a little wet in the very bottom.
Added coconut would probably double. Made more tonight with melted chocolate brushed on the crust then pressed shaved almonds in the chocolate. Almond joy pie now.

Just brought this to a birthday party for a friend who loves coconut - was a HUGE hit! But I did tweak the recipe a little: used a graham cracker crust, only 2 eggs, unsweetened coconut that I toasted first, and coconut milk instead of regular milk. Everyone raved about this so much that I had to comment. I use AllRecipes for almost everything I make - at least 3-4 times week - and this is the first time I've ever commented on a recipe. Thanks for sharing it!

Perfect Pie. I used a bit more coconut and packed the flakes down when measuring - using 1/2 of a 7oz. bag of Bakers Angel Flake sweetened coconut flakes and a 9" deep dish store bought crust. The mixture just fit into the pue crust and did not spill over during baking. I also lengthened the baking time by about 10 minutes (keeping a careful eye on the pie) to slightly brown the top, but this may just be because of differences between ovens. I LOVE coconut pie and this is an excellent one. I made it for a holiday dessert and everyone loved it. The pie was gobbled up. Easy to make with just a few ingredients. A new staple in my roster of pie recipes and desserts.
I packed the coconut as I measured it & covered with foil & cooked it 50 minutes at 325* then I toasted 1/2 cup of coconut & added it the last 10 minutes increase the temp to 350*

VERY GOOD. not like the eggy pudding type coconut pies from the store. THis was a cross between a pecan pie consistencywise and a coconut pie. I did change a few things: subbed 1 cup coconut milk for milk, toasted my coconut first and left out the vanilla. I also used a jiffy pie crust mix. Other than that the only change I would make is to cut a bit down on the sugar.
I made this according to instructions. Doubled everything for 2 pies. There was more filling that needed for 2 pies and cooked it according to directions and it was not done.
Love, love, love! Very buttery. I halved the recipe for hubs and I used mini graham cracker crusts. WOW!!

I like the simplicity of the recipe I did however make one change... Instead of regular milk I added a can of coconut milk and I used a plant based butter instead of a milk based butter (lactose free people in the house) the taste and looks of it are fabulous...
I followed the recipe for my first time. I was wondering what would coconut extract taste like instead of, or mixed with the vanilla.
My filling did not firm up? Any suggestions? I followed the recipe to the letter, please help!

I love this recipe!!! This is my first time baking, and this recipe is amazing! I am 12 years old and I baked it all by myself without my parents' help. My parents loved it and I enjoyed making it. The recipe is simple and convenient, I love it!

This recipe is exactly the same as my grandmother's recipe, which is probably 80 years old, I've been eating this recipe for 64 years and it is the best coconut pie you will ever find. I sprinkle coconut flakes on top to give a bit of toasted coconut flavor. THIS IS THE FINEST PIE A PERSON CAN EAT.
